events.title: Birth in Zakynthos
events.description: Niccolò Foscolo is born on Zakynthos, then under Venetian rule, to Andrea Foscolo, a physician, and Diamantina Spathis. He later adopts the name Ugo.

events.title: Death of his father
events.description: The death of Andrea Foscolo forces the family to leave Spalato. His mother moves to Venice to secure a future for her children.

events.title: Moves to Venice
events.description: Foscolo joins his mother in Venice, where he develops his literary interests and becomes involved in the city's intellectual and political circles.

events.title: The success of Tieste
events.description: His tragedy Tieste premieres at the Teatro di Sant'Angelo and receives a favourable public response, marking an important early success.

events.title: The Treaty of Campoformio
events.description: Napoleon cedes Venice to Austria. Foscolo sees the treaty as a betrayal of the republican ideals he supported and leaves Venice for Milan. The political disillusionment surrounding this event also informs the world of the Ortis.

events.title: The first printing of the Ortis begins
events.description: The Bologna printer and publisher Marsigli begins printing the Ultime lettere di Jacopo Ortis. The title page bears the date 1798, although the printing is not completed until the following year.

events.title: Vera storia di due amanti infelici
events.description: While Foscolo is away on military service, Marsigli entrusts the completion of the unfinished novel to Angelo Sassoli. The resulting publication appears under the title 'Vera storia di due amanti infelici ossia Ultime lettere di Jacopo Ortis'. Sassoli intervenes in the text, producing a version that does not represent Foscolo's intentions.

events.title: Foscolo disowns the first edition
events.description: Having learned of the publication completed in his absence, Foscolo publicly disowns the edition. This marks the beginning of his effort to reclaim control over the novel and establish an authoritative text.

events.title: The Mainardi Edition
events.description: Foscolo began a new, author-supervised edition of the Ortis, printed by the editor Mainardi in Milan. The project was interrupted due to some incomprensions between the author and the publisher. On 16 January 1802, Foscolo sent a copy to Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, which is now preserved in Weimar.

events.title: The Milan edition: Editio Princeps
events.description: Published by the Genio Tipografico publishing house, this edition presents a substantially revised version of the novel. Foscolo reworks its style, structure and characters, distancing himself from the unauthorised 1799 text. The editor's notice rejects the earlier editions and identifies the Milan edition as the authentic one.

events.title: Military service in France
events.description: Foscolo serves as an officer with the Italian troops stationed in France. He returns to Italy in 1806, continuing his literary work alongside his military career.

events.title: Publication of Dei Sepolcri
events.description: The poem 'Dei Sepolcri' is published by Nicolò Bettoni, consolidating Foscolo's reputation as one of the major Italian poets of his time.

events.title: Departure from Milan
events.description: Unwilling to swear allegiance to the Austrian emperor after the fall of Napoleon, Foscolo leaves Milan and goes into exile, first in Switzerland and later in England.

events.title: The Zurich edition
events.description: Published by Orell and Füssli in Zurich, this edition incorporates further material written during Foscolo's exile. It represents another stage in the novel's continuing textual development and precedes the definitive London edition. The place and date on this edition is London, 1814, even though it was printed in Zurich in 1816. This is a deliberate choice by Foscolo, who wanted to avoid political repercussions.

events.title: Arrival in London
events.description: Foscolo leaves Zurich on 27 July and reaches London after travelling through Basel. He settles among Italian exiles and British literary circles, where he continues to write and publish.

events.title: The London edition
events.description: John Murray publishes the last and new Ortis in London, divided in two volumes. This edition represents the culmination of Foscolo's long process of revision and establishes the form through which the novel became widely known.

events.title: Death in exile
events.description: Foscolo dies in exile near London. His remains are later transferred to Italy and buried in the Basilica of Santa Croce in Florence.
